Location.text: Multi-location - Sari (Taleghani Mahalleh village), Tehran, Rasht, and Qaem Shahr

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Paint Your Shadow Orange is a participatory project shaped by participants ranging from age 4 to 70, documented across video, image, and audio.
Centered around the concept of freedom, this project creates a space where each participant can present their own interpretation of the narrative.
This process leads to the formation of a collection of pluralistic actions and narratives that, alongside one another, form a narrative network.
Subsequently, these narratives are gathered in the form of a fabric canvas through needlework and patchwork.
This result is formed collectively and does not have a single creator; all participants, including the artist, are considered part of this network.

sections.title: Context & Site
paragraphs: The project has been executed in diverse settings;

From the space of the local and rural communities to an exhibition space at the Abie Boland Gallery in the city of Sari (Mazandaran Province), as well as in the format of exhibitions and workshops in other cities.
This project has also taken shape in domestic, public, and informal spaces and has been tried in any location where collective presence was possible.

sections.title: Motivations & Questions
paragraphs: This project was formed simultaneously with the publication of a story book and in relation to the social situation in Iran.
It was initiated from the urge to create a safe space for dialogue and hearing different narratives.
The project focuses on the process and the formation of peaceful dialogues within it, not on the final result or aesthetic concerns.
Among the main goals of the project, one was to create a connection with the audience and hearing the life narratives of individuals, especially in connection with the general public.
The project took shape in response to conditions in which crises such as Covid-19 and social and political turmoil had increased the need for reconnection and communal space.
Furthermore, the limitations of meeting in closed and formal spaces have driven artists towards creating other forms of interaction.
The lack of public spaces for free expression and dialogue was also among the influential factors in the formation of this project.

sections.title: Constraints & Strategies
paragraphs: Considering the subject of freedom as a central pillar to the project, there have been limitations in more public settings, and therefore no institutional support was possible.

In response to these conditions, the project initially began in a safer circle—including closed circles and the community around the Abie Boland Gallery — and later on has gradually expanded toward a wider public.
Moreover, the presence of children and adolescents in the project has significantly helped in shaping creative strategies along the way.

sections.title: Fundings & Partners
paragraphs: In collaboration with Abie Boland Gallery, Sepideh Pourreza, Solmaz Esmaeili, Afsaneh Sadeghi.
The project was initially funded and sponsored by the artist herself.
In later stages, during the final workshop in Qaem Shahr, the Ordibehesht Music Complex collaborated as a financial sponsor.

sections.title: About the Artist
paragraphs: Shima Raeeatparvar (born 1366, Sari) is an architecture graduate, researcher, and art instructor for children and adolescents based in Sari.

She is also a painter and a designer, Shima has been active in the field of visual arts for many years, and has participated in numerous group exhibitions.After establishing the Abie Boland Art Academy and Gallery, she has been working in her hometown with a focus on children and adolescents, designing and executing numerous projects in this context.

Instagram: shima.raeeatparvar / abie_boland_artacademy
Participation in this project has taken shape interactively and in the form of performance and installation.

Audiences could participate in the process according to their interest and inclination, from engaging in conversation and the process of writing & illustrating to participating in the sewing process and working directly with fabric.
The choice of the medium (sewing and working with fabric) was made in connection with the cultural and local context of the project.
Because of the proximity of these practices to the daily lives of the participants, it enhanced the chance of involving more active players.

The audience had a determining role in shaping the course of the project, and the artist acts more as a facilitator, working to provide conditions where participation can take place freely and without limitations.
